html:
The Polynesians are the peoples of the Pacific islands inside a great triangle with Hawaii, New Zealand and Rapa Nui (Easter Island) at its corners. On the map they hold the Hawaiian islands from 1000 to 1800.

They descend from Austronesian seafarers. The Lapita reached Tonga and Samoa around 900 to 800 BCE, and there a distinct Polynesian culture took shape. After a long pause came the settlement of East Polynesia, roughly 1000 to 1300 CE: the Society Islands, the Marquesas, Hawaii, Rapa Nui and finally New Zealand, settled by the Māori.

They sailed thousands of kilometres in double hulled canoes, steering by stars, swells and birds. They carried taro, breadfruit, coconuts, pigs, dogs and chickens. The sweet potato, from South America, shows that some voyagers reached the Americas and came back.

Their societies were ruled by chiefs with sacred power, mana, and guarded by rules of tapu, or kapu in Hawaii. Some grew into large chiefdoms, such as the Tuʻi Tonga network. On Rapa Nui people raised the moai.

In Hawaii, rival chiefdoms were growing into something like states when James Cook arrived in 1778. With Western guns, Kamehameha I united the islands into the Kingdom of Hawaii by 1810. In 1976 the canoe Hōkūleʻa sailed from Hawaii to Tahiti without instruments and helped revive the old way of navigating.
sum: The Polynesians are the peoples of the Pacific islands inside a great triangle with Hawaii, New Zealand and Rapa Nui (Easter Island) at its corners. On the map they hold the Hawaiian islands from 1000 to 1800.
